program_name: Economics and Data Analysis (Italian: Economia e analisi dei dati)
teaching_language: Mixed / partially English: Italian and English. The first two years are taught in ITALIAN; only the THIRD year is taught in English. This is NOT an English-taught programme and must not be presented as one. Italian language proficiency is required for admission and for the first two years of study.
campus: Brescia - Department of Economics and Management, University of Brescia (Italy)
degree_class: L-33 (Scienze economiche / Class of degrees in Economic Sciences)
english_delivery_scope: partial_third_year_english. The University of Brescia states that the language of instruction is Italian and English, with English used in the third year: 'the third year is taught in English'. The first two years are delivered in Italian. This means an international student without Italian cannot follow the programme from the start - the English component is a final-year exit track, not a full English-medium degree. Consistent with this, the programme does NOT appear as an English-taught bachelor's degree on the university's 'Study programmes taught in English' page, where Business and Economics is the English-taught bachelor's option in the Economics Area. The admission entrance test is the standard Italian-language TOLC-E (not the English CEnT-S), which further confirms Italian-medium entry. Any listing that classifies this programme as fully English is incorrect.
programme_status: active_first_year. The programme is newly activated: registration for the Economics and Data Analysis degree course became possible from academic year 2025/2026, and it continues to admit first-year students. It is an open-access (free access) programme with a compulsory but non-selective entrance test, so there is no numerus clausus, no ranking-based exclusion, and no phasing-out restriction on new applications. Enrolment for open-access undergraduate degree courses runs 13 July - 17 December 2026.
pre_evaluation_required: No dedicated PICA pre-evaluation is documented for this bachelor's programme. The University of Brescia's PICA-based pre-assessment procedure is explicitly scoped to non-EU candidates living abroad applying to master's (second-cycle) degrees, with a first round closing 15 March 2026 at noon Italian time; no equivalent undergraduate PICA pre-evaluation page was found. Non-EU candidates living abroad instead follow the standard route: a study-visa / pre-enrolment request on the Universitaly portal (deadline 31 August 2026), the Italian language test (see language_requirements), and submission of qualification documents to the International Students Office. [uncertain]
entry_test_name: TOLC-E (Test Online CISIA per l'Economia), delivered by CISIA in ITALIAN. It is compulsory but NON-SELECTIVE: it verifies basic preparation only and does not rank or exclude candidates. A score of at least 4/13 in the Mathematics section allows enrolment without an Additional Educational Obligation (OFA) in Mathematics; a lower score, or not sitting the test, results in an OFA in Mathematics being assigned, which does not prevent enrolment or class attendance. The test may be retaken at any CISIA-member university, including after enrolment, no later than 25 October, to clear the OFA. Note: the English-language variant (CEnT-S / English TOLC-E) is the test used for the separate, fully English-taught Business and Economics programme - not for this one. One indexed snippet ambiguously mentioned both TOLC-E and CEnT-S in connection with this programme, but the Italian-medium first two years and the dedicated TOLC-E page both point to TOLC-E as the applicable test. [uncertain]
admission_type: open access (free access / accesso libero) with a compulsory, non-selective CISIA entrance test (TOLC-E). No numerus clausus and no ranking-based selection; the test outcome only determines whether an Additional Educational Obligation (OFA) in Mathematics is assigned.
academic_requirements: A high school diploma (Italian upper-secondary leaving qualification) or a qualification obtained abroad and recognised as suitable under current Italian regulations. Possession of the prerequisites for successfully attending the course is verified at the start of the first year through the compulsory TOLC-E entrance test, focused on basic mathematics. Standard Italian bachelor's structure: 180 CFU over three years. Because the first two years are taught in Italian, applicants must be able to study in Italian from the outset; the English-medium component only begins in the third year. Applicants with foreign qualifications must have their qualification assessed for suitability by the International Students Office.
language_requirements: ITALIAN is the primary admission language requirement. Admission of foreign students is regulated by the Italian Ministry of University and Research 'Regulations for access of foreign students to university courses', which set out the procedures for verifying Italian language knowledge and the conditions for exemption. Non-EU candidates must prove Italian at CEFR level B2; for a.y. 2026/2027 the University of Brescia uses the CISIA TEST-ITALIANO-L2, held online in @CASA mode (from home or another location, via the CISIA portal on a personal computer or through the WEBEX virtual room on a smartphone). The registration fee is EUR 25 and the pass mark is 55/72. Only candidates who have already submitted their visa/pre-enrolment request on the Universitaly portal and selected a University of Brescia study programme are admitted to the test. IMPORTANT: the exemption from the Italian language test that applies to entirely English-taught programmes does NOT apply here, because this programme is only partially in English (third year). No specific English certificate (e.g. B2) is documented as an admission requirement, but students will need working English to follow the third year, which is delivered in English. [uncertain]
application_deadline_eu: Enrolment in open-access undergraduate degree courses is open from 13 July 2026 to 17 December 2026. The TOLC-E may be re-sat no later than 25 October to avoid or clear the Mathematics OFA. Requests for tuition-fee exemption or reduction must be submitted by 17 December 2026.
application_deadline_non_eu: Non-EU candidates resident abroad must submit and complete their study-visa / pre-enrolment request on the Universitaly portal by 31 August 2026, selecting University of Brescia and this programme, and must additionally pass the Italian language test (CISIA TEST-ITALIANO-L2) unless exempt. The university enrolment window itself remains 13 July - 17 December 2026. The Universitaly visa deadline is separate from, and earlier than, the enrolment deadline and must not be conflated with it. (The 15 March 2026 noon PICA pre-assessment deadline applies to master's degrees, not to this bachelor's programme.) [uncertain]
required_documents: High school diploma / foreign upper-secondary qualification; academic transcripts and certificates; TOLC-E result; proof of Italian language proficiency (CISIA TEST-ITALIANO-L2 pass at 55/72 or higher, or an accepted exemption under the Ministry's regulations for foreign students). For candidates holding foreign qualifications: documents legalised by the competent foreign authorities or bearing the Apostille stamp, plus either a Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore) issued by the Italian diplomatic representation or, as an alternative, a CIMEA Statement of Comparability; where required, a CIMEA Statement of Verification may substitute for legalisation. CIMEA statements are obtained via the Diplome online platform. The university recommends uploading diploma and certificates in Italian, French or English to speed up evaluation. International students must book an appointment with the International Students Office. Non-EU candidates abroad additionally need the Universitaly pre-enrolment/visa application. [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: Compulsory, non-selective, orientative entrance test: TOLC-E (Test Online CISIA per l'Economia), administered in Italian by CISIA and sittable at any CISIA-consortium university, on university premises or from home in TOLC@CASA mode. Its purpose is to verify basic preparation - principally mathematics - at the start of the first year. It does not rank, cap, or exclude candidates: the course has free access and an insufficient result does not prevent enrolment in the degree programme or attendance of classes. Outcome: at least 4/13 in the Mathematics section means enrolment without an Additional Educational Obligation (OFA); below that threshold, or if the test is not sat, an OFA in Mathematics is assigned and must subsequently be cleared. The test may be repeated at any CISIA-associated university, even after enrolment, no later than 25 October, to avoid attribution of the Mathematics OFA. No interview or personal-preparation assessment is documented.

Declaration of value prepared by Italian Representation or alternatively the Statement of comparability issued by CIMEA.

uncertainty_notes:
ACCESS LIMITATION (primary caveat): unibs.it and corsi.unibs.it are protected by a Cloudflare/human-verification bot challenge. Direct retrieval failed on every attempt - WebFetch returned HTTP 405 for corsi.unibs.it URLs and HTTP 403 for www.unibs.it URLs and unibs.it-hosted PDFs. A real browser session loaded only a 'Human Verification / Let's confirm you are human' interstitial; the challenge was deliberately NOT completed (bypassing bot detection is out of scope). All content was therefore compiled from search-engine indexed snippets of those same official unibs.it / corsi.unibs.it pages, and NO page was directly verified. Field values should be re-checked against the live pages before publication.

ENGLISH SCOPE - HIGH CONFIDENCE, CRITICAL: Multiple independent indexed snippets from corsi.unibs.it consistently state that the language is 'Italian and English (third year)' and that 'the third year is taught in English'. The programme is absent from the university's English-taught programmes listing, and its entrance test is the Italian-language TOLC-E rather than the English CEnT-S. This programme must be classified as partial_third_year_english and must NOT be marketed or imported as a fully English-taught degree. Prospective international students without Italian cannot begin this programme.

SPECIFIC UNCERTAINTIES:
1. entry_test_name / entry_exam_or_test: One indexed snippet of the programme page mentioned both 'the TOLC-E (Test Online CISIA per l'Economia) and the CEnT-S (CISIA English Test for Sciences)' in relation to this course. This is most likely either indexing bleed from the sibling Business and Economics page or a dual-option provision, but it could not be resolved without direct page access. The dedicated unibs TOLC-E page explicitly names Economics and Data Analysis L-33 as a TOLC-E course, so TOLC-E is recorded as the applicable test. Confirm with the department whether CEnT-S is also accepted.
2. language_requirements: No English certificate requirement was found for this programme, in contrast to the explicit B2 requirement for Business and Economics. Whether an English level is required or recommended before the third year (which is English-taught) could not be confirmed. The Italian B2 / TEST-ITALIANO-L2 details come from the university-wide non-EU admissions pages rather than the programme page itself, and exemption conditions under the Ministry's regulations were not enumerated.
3. pre_evaluation_required: All located PICA pre-assessment material at unibs.it is explicitly scoped to master's/second-cycle degrees (first round closing 15 March 2026, noon). No undergraduate PICA pre-evaluation page was found, so 'not required' is an inference from absence of evidence rather than a positive confirmation.
4. application_deadline_non_eu: The 31 August 2026 Universitaly study-visa deadline is a university-wide non-EU deadline, not one confirmed on this programme's page. The Italian language test date/registration windows were also not located.
5. application_deadline_eu: The 13 July - 17 December 2026 window is the general open-access undergraduate enrolment window; a programme-specific call page for Economics and Data Analysis was not directly verified. Because the programme launched in 2025/2026 and the current date is September 2026, this window most plausibly refers to a.y. 2026/2027, but the academic year is not stated explicitly in the retrieved snippets.
6. required_documents: Compiled from the university's general international-admissions and CIMEA pages rather than a programme-specific checklist.
7. campus: Brescia is confirmed (the corsi.unibs.it page is titled 'Economics and Data Analysis - Brescia'); the specific teaching building was not confirmed, though the Department of Economics and Management (Via San Faustino 74/B, Brescia) is the relevant department.
8. official_call_url: https://corsi.unibs.it/en/data-analysis/enrolling appeared in search results as the programme's enrolling page but could not be opened directly. An alternate programme URL https://corsi.unibs.it/en/dataanalysis also resolves to the same course.
9. tuition_or_fees_link: Points to the general university fees page; no programme-specific fee schedule was located. The 2026/2027 fee regulations extend the 'no tax' exemption threshold to an ISEE of EUR 28,000, with further reductions at higher ISEE bands.
